issues.description: In class Stock the method used to add a StockIngredient is named differently between the problem statement/solution and the template. The problem statement's UML declares Stock.addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient): void (problem_statement.md line 53). The reference solution implements Stock.addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java line 18). The template implementation instead provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient) (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java line 18). This naming mismatch can cause compilation errors or confusion when students follow the UML or solution examples and try to call addToStockIngredients on the provided template Stock class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across artifacts. Either (a) rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), or (b) add a forwarding method public void addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient ingredient) { addItem(ingredient); } in the template. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to use addItem if that name is preferred. Ensure the method name used in the UML, template, and solution match so students do not get compilation errors.
